tasks.short: Read the work order to find the product, quantity and specifications, look up the recipe and mixing instructions, and check raw material lots against the order.

steps.what: Mixer operator reads work orders to determine production specifications: on paper today, on the line terminal after the change
Mixer operator looks up the recipe and mixing instructions in the binder
Mixer operator checks raw material lots against the order

tasks.design: The work order shows on the line terminal of the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with the recipe, mixing steps and limits for that product, so the operator does not search binders. Scanning each raw material lot checks it against the recipe and flags a wrong or expired lot. Reading and understanding the order stays with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Work orders were paper and recipes sat in binders at the line.
tasks.enabler_now: Production systems show orders and recipes on line terminals and check lots by barcode.
tasks.still_hard: Special orders need notes from the shift leader that are not in the system.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a raw material looks different from last week's lot.

reach.learn: Whether wrong lots are stopped before mixing.

evidence.claim: Critical Manufacturing MES computes recipe parameters by business rules and runs SPC and defect capture.
Systems that can monitor staff presence, behaviour or performance, such as per-operator logs, need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the work order to materials checked; weighing and mixing are outside.
Input contract: orders from planning; recipes kept by quality; fallback is paper orders and binders.
Reading the order keeps its full time. s2 keeps 20 for reading the recipe on screen and for special orders with notes outside the system; s3 keeps 50 because each lot is still handled and scanned.
Raw materials carry barcodes from the supplier or goods receipt.

incremental.description: Mixer operator reports lots with unreadable labels.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many special orders with notes outside the system and lots without barcodes, so binders and hand checks stay for many batches (18.0); high: recipes kept by quality and lots barcoded as assumed (33.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Walk the line to observe production and monitor mixers, read gauges against limits, and adjust or stop the machine when something is out of limits.

steps.what: Mixer operator observes production and monitors equipment on rounds
Mixer operator reads gauges and compares them with limits
Mixer operator adjusts or stops the machine to ensure safe and efficient operation

tasks.design: Temperatures, speeds, pressures and mixing times from the machine controls show on one screen with control charts and alarm limits ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the operator reads fewer gauges by hand and is called to the mixer that drifts. Rounds to see, hear and smell the line stay, and adjusting or stopping a machine stays with the operator; nothing adjusts the machine by itself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Gauges were read one by one on rounds.
tasks.enabler_now: SPC software reads machine controls and raises alarms on control charts.
tasks.still_hard: Leaks, smells and odd noises do not show on a screen.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a mixer bearing start to go before the alarm.

evidence.claim: Q-DAS O-QIS reads gauges and PLCs, shows control charts and raises alarms.
AI as a safety component of machinery is high-risk under Article 6(1); alarm limits here are fixed rules, not a safety function.

assumptions: Boundary: from the running batch to the machine adjusted; repairs are outside.
Input contract: machine controls connected to the SPC system; limits set by process engineering; fallback is gauge rounds.
Adjusting and stopping stay with the operator.
Rounds continue for leaks, smells and noise and keep their full time; s2 keeps 40 because most gauge values show on the screen and the rest are read on rounds.

incremental.description: Mixer operator answers and logs alarms.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only a few machine controls are connected, so most gauges are still read on rounds (4.7); high: controls connected as assumed (13.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record batch weights, times and temperatures on the batch form, compute totals and yield, note deviations, check the batch record, and hand it to quality.

steps.what: Mixer operator records weights, times and temperatures: copied onto the batch form today; after the change scales and machine controls send them and the operator confirms each weighing on the display
Mixer operator computes totals and yield on the form
Mixer operator notes deviations and manual additions: on the paper forms today, in the electronic batch record after the change
Mixer operator checks the completed batch record: weights, times and temperatures against the recipe and limits, and that every deviation and manual addition is noted
Mixer operator signs and releases the checked batch record to quality: handed over on paper today, by one release in the production system after the change

tasks.design: Weights from connected scales and times and temperatures from the machine controls go into the electronic batch record in the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), which computes totals and yield. The operator writes deviations and manual additions in the record, checks it, and signs and releases it once to quality. Checking the record stays with the operator; per-operator logs are not used to rate staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were copied from displays onto paper forms and totals worked out by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Production systems take readings from scales and machine controls and compute totals.
tasks.still_hard: Manual additions and rework still need careful notes.
tasks.human_edge: Writing a deviation note that quality can follow the next morning.
tasks.altitude: The operator checks records instead of writing them.

evidence.claim: Critical Manufacturing MES computes recipe parameters by business rules and captures defects.
Systems that can monitor staff performance, such as per-operator logs, need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the running batch to the record with quality; batch release is outside.
Input contract: scales and machine controls connected; forms set by quality; fallback is paper forms.

Checking the record, writing deviations and manual additions, and the release stay with the operator. s1 keeps 10 for confirming each weighing; s2 goes because the system computes totals and yield, which the check in s4 reads; s5 keeps 10 for the release itself.
Quality accepts the electronic batch record.
research_questions: Do batch records with errors fall?

incremental.description: Mixer operator corrects readings when a scale connection fails.

approvals.approved_version: The batch record exactly as checked by the operator in s4, signed and released once to quality's review queue in the production system; any later change needs a new check and release.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of the scales and controls are not connected, so half of the readings are still copied and totalled by hand (32.5); high: scales and controls connected as assumed (58.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The mixer operator keeps reading orders, watching the line and adjusting machines; binders, gauge rounds and paper batch forms shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An operator who spends saved time on the line and on problem solving.

job.title: Mixing and Blending Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
